title: ShadowLeak: zero-click exfiltration from ChatGPT Deep Research runs inside OpenAI's cloud
summary: Radware researchers Gabi Nakibly, Zvika Babo and Maor Uziel showed that an email carrying hidden instructions in tiny or white-on-white text could make ChatGPT's Deep Research agent, working through its Gmail connector, send personal data such as an employee's name and address to an attacker-controlled URL with no user interaction, with the actions running on OpenAI's cloud servers rather than the user's device. Radware reported the flaw to OpenAI through Bugcrowd on 18 June; OpenAI said it was fixed in early August and marked it resolved on 3 September, and Radware said it had not seen the vulnerability exploited in the wild.
